questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 1.
questions.solution: As per the context, the statement is of negative connotation and the blank should convey the same tone. Damper- a person or thing that has a subduing or inhibiting effect, will be a perfect fit here. While other options convey positivity, some of them do not make any sense at all. Hence, b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.
questions.solution: The sentence talks about two different options- one, letting things get in the way and second, pushing them out (it's giving a choice); hence, (d) is the right answer. Other options do not make sense here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.
questions.solution: A continuous form of the verb is to be used as the context talks about something that has been in continuation. (b) and (d) are eliminated. (c) doesn't make any sense. 'Investing' is contextually and grammatically correct; hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 4.
questions.solution: The relative pronoun refers to the nearest noun; which in this case is 'people' (it's a living thing and not an object; for objects we use the pronoun 'which'). Hence, the pronoun suited for it is 'who'; hence, (b) is the right answer. (c) and (d) do not make sense and are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 5.
questions.solution: The author talks about how he/she has a list of things to which he/she refers to when things are not going his/her way. The only contextually and grammatically option is 'wrong'; hence, (c) is the right answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:

Harnessing: to control and make use of something, typically a natural resource or energy, for a particular purpose.

Testifying: to provide evidence or proof in support of something.

Amplifying: to make something larger, louder, or more significant.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:

Ambitious: having a strong desire to achieve something significant or challenging.

Superstitious: believing in supernatural causality, where certain events are believed to be the result of supernatural forces rather than natural or scientific explanations.

Nutritious: providing nourishment and promoting good health.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.

Terminate: to bring to an end or to stop something.

Stimulate: to encourage or arouse interest or activity in something.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:

Symbol: something that represents or stands for something else, often an idea, concept, or characteristic.

questions.solution: An adverb is needed in the blank to modify the adjective 'vulnerable'. Inherently- in a way that exists as a natural or basic part of something. Option C is the correct answer. All the other options are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question: Which word/phrase should come at (B)?
questions.solution: A noun will take the place of the blank. Jeorpardy- danger of loss, harm, or failure; danger; peril. Option C is the correct answer. All the other options are grammatically incorrect (as they all are adjectives)

questions.question: Which word/phrase should come at (D)?
questions.solution: A noun will replace the blank. Commercialization- the process of managing or running something principally for financial gain. It is the best choice for the blank. Option D is the correct answer. All the other options are grammatically incorrect.

All the other options are grammatically or contextually incorrect.

questions.question: Which of the following words can replace the blank marked as (1) in the passage?
questions.solution: Statue - a carved or cast figure of a person or animal, especially one that is life-size or larger. Stature - height or position. State - condition. Status - social or professional position. Going by contextual understanding, only A makes sense here.

questions.question: Which of the following words can replace the blank marked as (2) in the passage?
questions.solution: Coronation - the ceremony where a prince or king is crowned. Tribute - honour. Vowed - took an oath or promised. We need a verb here, so A and C are incorrect as they are nouns. It is incorrect to say that someone was vowed; one can only vow to do something, not someone. D is incorrect, and B is the right answer.

questions.question: Which of the following words can replace the blank marked as (3) in the passage?
questions.solution: Course - journey or direction. Voyaged - travelled. Coarse - rough. Discourse - discussion. We need a noun here, so B and C are incorrect as the former is a verb, and the latter, an adjective. 'Discourse' makes no sense here, as the context is not talking of a discussion. A is the right answer.

questions.question: Which of the following words can replace the blank marked as (4) in the passage?
questions.solution: Restrain - control. Constraint - force. Desire - wish. We need a noun here, so A is incorrect as it is a verb. Note that the sentence construction says: 'not by _____ but of our own will'. This suggests that an antonym of 'will' must be used. D is the right answer.

questions.question: Which of the following words can replace the blank marked as (5) in the passage?
questions.solution: Rein - straps used to restrain a horse. Inland - situated in the interior of a country rather than on the coast. We need a noun here, so A is incorrect as it is an adjective. Likewise, for D, which is also an adjective or adverb. B is the right answer, which makes greatest sense in the given context.
